fact: Vodacom Congo, the operator itself, says it spends on average USD 140 million a year on its network in the DRC and plans a long-term programme of USD 670 million, as stated at the Vodacom Impact Forum on 8 October 2026; the document does not say where the financier is from.

EAAIF, a PIDG fund managed by Ninety One in London, signed a USD 32.8 million senior secured loan to Eastcastle Infrastructure DRC, within an upsized USD 179 million facility, to build 728 towers in the DRC; the Liquid Intelligent Technologies loan is multi-country with no DRC amount and is not counted.

Helios Towers DRC signed an investment agreement with the national investment promotion agency ANAPI on 31 March 2026 for more than USD 100 million in shared telecom towers, which the company itself says it is investing; the document does not say where the company is from.

PIDG's Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF) committed a USD 30 million commercial loan to Eastcastle Infrastructure, a DRC telecom tower platform, with activity start in June 2023; the document later records a 2026 refinancing of the same exposure, not an additional one.
